title: Burst usage UI in Console (graphs, limit indicators, warning states)
creator: Alicia Perez
description:
Goal
Design the Dedicated Console UI for the new “Burst Capacity” option. Customers should be able to answer:
1) Am I bursting right now?
2) How much burst did I use today/this week (and when)?
3) What are my limits (baseline vs burst cap), and why am I getting denials/429s?
4) Are there risk states (cooldown, fleet safety, pool saturation) that will affect my workload?

Scope
- Burst usage graphs (time series) with clear distinction between baseline reserved usage vs burst usage.
- Limit indicators: baseline allocation, burst cap, remaining headroom, and the configured max burst ratio.
- Warning & degraded states: burst denied, burst capped, cooldown active, pool saturated / global circuit breaker, telemetry lag.
- “Explain this” affordances for denial reason codes so Support/CS can point customers to a single view.

Non-goals
- Full billing invoice UI (Finance will handle line items elsewhere). We only show usage estimates and point to billing exports.
- Cross-region bursting UX (out of scope for v1).

Primary surfaces
1) Dedicated → Capacity → Burst (new tab) on a tenant’s dedicated cluster page.
2) Dedicated → Overview (small “Burst status” card + deep link).

Key UX principles
- Make burst optional and legible: show baseline as the stable contract, burst as temporary/conditional.
- Avoid implying hard guarantees: burst availability depends on pool health and guardrails.
- Provide actionable debugging: clear denial reasons, what to try next, and when to escalate.

Proposed information architecture
A) Header: “Burst Capacity”
- Toggle status: Enabled/Disabled (read-only for most users; change via admin/support)
- Current state pill: Normal | Bursting | Capped | Denied | Cooldown | Degraded (pool)
- Last config change (timestamp) + “View audit log” link (if available)

B) ‘Current limits’ section (compact)
- Baseline reserved capacity: X GPUs (or equivalent throughput unit as provided by Dedicated)
- Burst cap: up to Y GPUs (or +Z% / ratio)
- Headroom now: numeric + small bar indicator (baseline portion + burst portion)
- Cooldown window: e.g., “10 min cooldown after 15 min burst at cap” (exact policy text is driven by config)

C) Main chart: “Usage over time”
- Stacked area chart (preferred): baseline usage (solid) + burst usage (striped overlay)
- Time ranges: 1h, 6h, 24h (default), 7d
- Hover tooltip includes:
  - Baseline used
  - Burst used
  - Burst admitted vs denied counts (if available at that granularity)
  - Notes when circuit breaker / pool saturation is active
- Annotations overlay for events: config change, rollout gate change, circuit breaker activation, major denial spikes

D) Secondary chart: “Burst denials”
- Bar chart of denials over time (same range selector)
- Breakdown dropdown: by denial reason code (top 5 + “other”), by route/model (if label cardinality safe), by region/hardware class

E) Table: “Denial reasons (last 24h)”
- Columns: Reason, Count, First seen, Last seen, Recommended action
- Recommended actions are short, deterministic, and avoid hand-wavy guidance.

Reason code copy (v1)
- FLEET_SAFETY_CAP: “Burst is temporarily limited to protect overall fleet reliability. Retry with backoff; contact Support if sustained.”
- POOL_SATURATED: “Burst pool is saturated in this region/hardware class. Reduce concurrency or shift workload timing.”
- TENANT_BURST_CAP_REACHED: “You hit your configured burst cap. Increase cap (contract change) or scale baseline.”
- COOLDOWN_ACTIVE: “Cooldown window active after sustained burst usage. Burst will resume after cooldown.”
- POLICY_DENY: “Burst request denied by policy (ratio/guardrail).”
- TELEMETRY_LAG_PROTECTION: “Burst temporarily constrained due to delayed capacity signals. Typically clears quickly.”

Warning and degraded states (behavior)
- If burst is enabled but currently unavailable (pool degraded / circuit breaker): show a yellow banner at top with last updated timestamp.
- If telemetry lag > threshold (as provided by SRE): show a small “Data delayed” badge near charts; avoid showing precise “headroom now” and instead show “headroom (estimated)”.
- If the Console API is stale: show “Last refreshed at …” and a manual refresh CTA; do not silently show old limits.

Accessibility
- Color is not the only signal: use patterns (striped burst overlay), icons for state pills, and clear text labels.
- Ensure chart legends are keyboard navigable and tooltips have a tab-accessible summary.

Data requirements (from Eng)
- Timeseries: baseline_usage, burst_usage (same unit), plus optional admitted/denied counts
- Config: baseline allocation, burst cap (absolute and/or ratio), cooldown policy summary, enabled flag, priority tier (optional)
- Health flags: pool_saturation, fleet_safety_active, telemetry_lag_seconds
- Denials: reason_code, count, window; optionally per-route aggregation (guarded by cardinality)

Deliverables
- Figma frames for: Normal/Bursting, Cap reached, Denied (with reason), Cooldown, Degraded (circuit breaker), Telemetry lag, Empty state.
- Copy spec for banners, tooltips, and denial reason “recommended action”.
- Instrumentation notes: ensure we log which warnings are shown to validate comprehension during beta.

Rollout note
Design supports beta with limited regions/hardware classes. Where burst is not available in a region, show ‘Not available in this region’ with guidance to contact CSM (no self-serve switching).
acceptance_criteria: Customer can distinguish baseline vs burst usage in the main time series without reading docs
UI clearly shows configured burst cap and when it is reached (not just ‘429’)
Denial reason codes are human-readable and include a recommended action that Support agrees with
Degraded states (pool saturation, fleet safety) are explicit and do not imply an SLA guarantee
Telemetry lag/staleness is surfaced; UI does not present stale limits as current truth
Design spec includes empty states and error states for missing/partial data
design_notes: Chart choice: stacked area outperformed two-line chart in quick internal preference test because it reads as ‘baseline is always there; burst is the extra’. Burst overlay uses pattern fill to stay readable in grayscale.

Units: the UI labels usage in the same unit Dedicated uses for capacity in Console today (GPU-equivalent). Where we only have burst ‘GPU-seconds’ from metering, we show it as ‘Burst usage (GPU-sec)’ in the Denials/Reporting subpanel, not in the primary capacity chart.
Headroom: we show headroom as ‘up to’ and avoid precise promises when pool health is degraded; copy includes ‘subject to pool availability and guardrails’.
We intentionally keep per-model breakdown behind a dropdown and default off due to label/cardinality constraints raised by Observability.
review_comments: 2025-02-10 (Lauren Bishop, Product): Please ensure the UI does not read like a guaranteed on-demand add-on. We need language that matches contract stance: ‘best effort within guardrails’ + clear denial explanations.

2025-02-11 (Chloe Martin, Console backend): Confirm we can provide baseline + burst timeseries at 1m and 5m resolution. Per-route breakdown might be limited to top-N routes to keep cardinality manageable.

2025-02-12 (Sean Gallagher, SRE): Add a ‘fleet safety / circuit breaker’ state that is unmistakable and timestamped. Also, we need a ‘telemetry delayed’ indicator to prevent customers from screenshotting incorrect headroom numbers during lag incidents.

2025-02-13 (Mina Haddad, Routing): Please reflect that some denials will manifest as immediate 429s and some as backpressure/queuing depending on admission semantics. UI should avoid promising a single behavior; keep it in ‘recommended action’ copy.
2025-02-14 (Allison Grant, Observability): Avoid high-cardinality labels by default. Prefer reason-code breakdown first; allow model/route breakdown only when we can guarantee stable label sets.

2025-02-18 (Rachel Kim, CS): Add a ‘Copy debug info’ action (tenant, region, time range, top denial reasons) to reduce back-and-forth in support tickets. Even if v1 is manual text copy, place the affordance.

2025-02-20 (Ethan Park, Control plane): ‘Enabled/Disabled’ should be shown as read-only unless user has appropriate permissions. Also, show last config change timestamp to help diagnose propagation delays.
decision_log: 2025-02-12: Selected stacked area chart with patterned burst overlay for baseline vs burst usage.
2025-02-13: Added explicit degraded states for global circuit breaker and telemetry lag per SRE feedback.
2025-02-18: Added ‘Copy debug info’ affordance and a denial reason table optimized for Support workflows.
2025-02-21: Finalized denial reason copy to align with reason codes coming from ENG (no custom Console-only categories).
open_questions: Do we show ‘estimated cost of burst’ in Console v1, or defer entirely to billing exports? (Product leaning: defer, but show link to usage report export.)
Do we expose priority tier (gold/silver) in the UI? Currently hidden unless Support view is enabled to avoid customer-to-customer comparison.
What is the minimum safe refresh interval / caching behavior to avoid SUP-28541 style ‘stale config’ tickets? Need final guidance from Console backend + control plane.
